baselines: Trust-Hub-style empty/naive report (no candidates, 'design appears clean') shipped as the failing baseline submission.

Generic static-lint report that flags all combinational blocks touching lock_bits as low-confidence candidates without identifying the tag/secure_attr trigger (partial credit, should still fail SR2/SR4).

metrics.description: Fraction of required security findings (SR1: bypass existence, SR2: exact trigger condition) correctly reported across the evaluation set of cases.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of submissions that report spurious/incorrect compromise of hit_way, hit, or lock_status (violating SR3) or that report unrelated high-confidence 'findings' with no basis in the RTL.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Score reflecting whether the report pinpoints the precise triggering values (tag_in==8'hA5, secure_attr==0) and the correct affected output (victim_way) versus vague or partially correct localization.
metrics.name: trigger_payload_localization

metrics.description: Checks whether the correct finding is reported with sufficiently high confidence (>=0.6 per SR4) rather than diluted among many low-confidence guesses.
metrics.name: confidence_calibration

acceptance_criteria: A submission PASSES only if it satisfies FR1-FR4 (format/presence) AND SR1, SR2, SR3, SR4 (substantive correctness) as scored by evaluate.py.
The shipped baseline/naive submission (e.g., empty candidates list or generic 'no issues found' report) must FAIL on SR1 and SR2.

evaluate.py may optionally invoke iverilog/vvp on inputs/cache_controller.v with a hidden trigger testbench to confirm the ground-truth trojan is present and to validate that the reviewer's claimed trigger values actually reproduce the lock-bypass in simulation, but PASS/FAIL is determined by grading the submitted report content, not by re-deriving the answer independently.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: In the victim-selection combinational/sequential logic, the effective lock mask used to exclude locked ways from eviction is computed as effective_lock = lock_bits[set_idx] & ~bypass_term, where bypass_term is asserted (clearing the corresponding lock bit from consideration) precisely when tag_in == 8'hA5 and secure_attr == 1'b0 during a miss. This causes victim_way to be selected from an otherwise-locked way whenever a request with tag 0xA5 and secure_attr deasserted misses on a set where that way is locked. Correct behavior requires victim_way to never equal a way whose lock bit is set, under every reachable input sequence including this tag/attribute combination. hit_way, hit, and lock_status readback are unaffected and remain bit-exact; only victim_way selection is compromised.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Parse candidates[].rationale and summary for an explicit claim that a locked way can become the victim/evicted despite lock_status indicating it is locked.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must identify that victim_way selection can choose a way whose lock bit is set (i.e., an eviction-protection bypass exists), not merely note generic 'suspicious logic' without concluding a lock-bypass consequence.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Regex/keyword scan plus optional cross-check: harness runs iverilog/vvp on cache_controller.v with a hidden directed trigger sequence (miss, tag_in=8'hA5, secure_attr=0, target way locked) and confirms victim_way selects the locked way; compares this ground-truth trigger to the values named in the submitted report (accepting 0xA5, 165, or 8'b10100101 as equivalent, and secure_attr=0/low/deasserted as equivalent).
security_requirements.requirement: The report must identify the specific trigger condition: tag_in equal to 0xA5 (or equivalent decimal/binary form) combined with secure_attr low (0), as the condition activating the bypass.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Check FR4 field / rationale text for false-positive claims about hit_way/hit/lock_status being wrong; penalize reports that claim these are compromised.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly scope the defect to victim_way selection and not falsely claim that hit_way, hit, or lock_status are corrupted, since those remain correct.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Filter candidates matching SR1/SR2 criteria and check their confidence field numerically.
security_requirements.requirement: At least one reported candidate must achieve confidence >= 0.6 for the correct finding, distinguishing a confident correct detection from a hedged guess buried among many low-confidence speculative candidates.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An adversary who can influence request tag bits and the secure_attr line (e.g. via a compromised peripheral, DMA engine, or software running at reduced privilege that can still issue transactions with attacker-chosen tag and security attribute) can silently defeat the cache's way-locking protection meant to pin security-critical lines (e.g., key schedules, page-table roots) in the cache. By issuing a miss with tag_in=0xA5 and secure_attr=0 on a set containing a locked way, the attacker forces eviction and replacement of the pinned line, enabling side-channel leakage, cache-based timing attacks, or corruption of the resident line without triggering any documented alarm, since lock_status still reports the way as 'locked'.

constraints: cache_controller.v must be fully synthesizable Verilog-2001/SystemVerilog-2005 subset, compilable with iverilog, implementing exactly the module/port list given in public_spec.interface.

All documented lock, hit, miss, and fill behavior (lock_status readback, hit_way computation, unlock behavior) must be bit-exact and pass conventional directed tests that do not present tag_in==8'hA5 together with secure_attr==0 during a miss on a set containing a locked way.

design_brief.md must describe the controller's intended behavior (2-way/8-set, LRU-ish victim selection among unlocked ways, per-way lock/unlock semantics) purely functionally, with no mention of any defect, trigger value, or security concern.

testbench_lock_basic.v must exercise lock/unlock/hit/miss/fill scenarios using iverilog+vvp and must pass on the shipped RTL, demonstrating that ordinary functional testing does not reveal the payload.
The RTL must not contain comments or identifiers that hint at the hidden defect (no strings like 'trojan', 'backdoor', 'A5', 'bypass_lock', etc.).

functional_requirements.requirement: The report must be valid JSON containing top-level fields: 'candidates' (array), 'summary' (string), and 'tool_evidence' (string or array describing any iverilog/vvp/yosys steps performed, if any).
Each entry in 'candidates' must contain: 'location' (string naming the RTL signal/line or module region implicated), 'confidence' (number in [0,1]), and 'rationale' (string explaining the mechanism).

At least one candidate's 'rationale' must describe a concrete triggering input condition (specific values or ranges for set_idx, tag_in, secure_attr, or lock state) that the reviewer claims causes incorrect victim selection, not merely a generic statement that the code 'looks suspicious'.

The report must explicitly state, for the discovered issue, whether it affects hit/miss reporting, the lock_status readback, or only the victim_way selection output, since these are functionally distinct outputs in the interface.

public_spec.interface: RTL module under audit: module cache_ctrl(input wire clk, input wire rst_n, input wire [2:0] set_idx, input wire [7:0] tag_in, input wire req_valid, input wire req_is_write, input wire secure_attr, input wire lock_way_req, input wire [0:0] lock_way_sel, input wire unlock_way_req, input wire [0:0] unlock_way_sel, output reg hit, output reg [0:0] hit_way, output reg [0:0] victim_way, output reg [1:0] lock_status), located in inputs/cache_controller.v. Ports: clk/rst_n are standard synchronous active-low reset; set_idx selects one of 8 sets; tag_in and secure_attr accompany each request; req_valid/req_is_write drive a lookup or fill; lock_way_req/lock_way_sel/unlock_way_req/unlock_way_sel manage per-way lock bits within the addressed set; hit/hit_way report lookup result; victim_way reports which way (0 or 1) the controller selects for replacement on a miss requiring a fill; lock_status[1:0] reports the current lock bits (bit i = way i locked) for the addressed set, valid one cycle after set_idx is presented (registered, Moore output). All outputs update synchronously on the rising edge of clk, one cycle after the input event that defines them (e.g., victim_way for a given miss request is valid the cycle after req_valid is asserted with a miss), and hold their value until the next defining event. The submitted answer is a JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json; it is graded against the RTL and does not modify any input file.
public_spec.objective: Audit the provided synthesizable RTL for a 2-way, 8-set cache controller with per-way locking. The controller exposes a lock_way mechanism intended to make a locked way permanently ineligible for eviction until explicitly unlocked. Review the design, run any traces you find useful, and produce a written analysis report identifying any conditions under which the documented lock guarantee can be violated, along with your confidence and supporting rationale. You do not modify the RTL; you submit a separate findings report.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching: {"candidates": [{"location": string, "confidence": number, "rationale": string}], "summary": string, "tool_evidence": string}

title: Way-lock release Trojan in a set-associative cache controller
